title: Archives (tar)
intro: Work from the module directory. Use **`tar`** (and **`find`** / **`wc`** / **`sort`** where helpful). Extract only under **`work/`**. On macOS BSD `tar`, put **`-C directory`** immediately before **`-xf archive`**.

questions.prompt: List all member paths in **`m13_lab.tar`**, sorted alphabetically.
Extract **`m13_lab.tar`** into an empty `work/m13b/` directory. What is the first line of `work/m13b/nested/num.txt`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
mkdir -p work/m13b
tar -C work/m13b -xf m13_lab.tar
head -n1 work/m13b/nested/num.txt
```

questions.prompt: Extract only the `readme.txt` member from **`m13_lab.tar`** into a fresh `work/m13c/` directory. How many regular files end up in `work/m13c` after extraction?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
mkdir -p work/m13c
tar -C work/m13c -xf m13_lab.tar readme.txt
find work/m13c -type f | wc -l
```

questions.prompt: **`m13_lab.tar.gz`** is a gzip-compressed version of the archive. How many members does it contain?
List the members of **`m13_lab.tar.gz`**. Which member is stored inside a subdirectory?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
tar -tzf m13_lab.tar.gz | sort
```

`nested/num.txt` is the only member with a directory path component.

questions.prompt: Create a new archive `work/mini.tar` containing only `readme.txt` from the module directory. What member path does listing the archive show?
Extract all members of **`m13_lab.tar`** into a fresh `work/m13f/` directory. How many regular files are created?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
rm -rf work/m13f && mkdir -p work/m13f
tar -C work/m13f -xf m13_lab.tar
find work/m13f -type f | wc -l
```

questions.prompt: After the extraction in the previous question, list all regular files under `work/m13f`. Which file is inside a subdirectory? Give its path relative to `work/m13f`.
Print the first line of the `readme.txt` member from **`m13_lab.tar`** without writing anything to disk.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
tar -xOf m13_lab.tar readme.txt | head -n1
```

`-O` sends member content to stdout instead of creating a file.

questions.prompt: Create a bzip2-compressed archive **`work/compressed.tar.bz2`** using the source files in **`m13_tree/`**. How many members does the resulting archive contain?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
tar -cjf work/compressed.tar.bz2 -C m13_tree .
tar -tjf work/compressed.tar.bz2 | wc -l
```

`-j` selects bzip2 compression. List with `-t` to verify member count.

questions.prompt: `mystery.tar.gz` is in the module directory. List its contents carefully — there may be hidden members. Extract and print only the hidden file's content without writing it to disk.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
tar tf mystery.tar.gz
# report.txt
# .barnacle
tar xOf mystery.tar.gz .barnacle
```

`tar tf` lists all members including dotfiles. `-O` (stdout) extracts directly to stdout without creating a file on disk — useful for reading a single member from an untrusted archive.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Create and extract archives; choose compression flags (`z`, `j`, `J`, `--zstd` on modern GNU `tar`).
- Understand `tar` path semantics: trailing slash, absolute paths danger (`--absolute-names` caution).
- Preserve or intentionally strip permissions and ownership.
- List contents without extracting (`-t`) and extract single members.

## Scope

**In scope:** `tar` as the universal archive CLI. **Out of scope:** `cpio`/`pax` full mastery except as forward pointers.
